paper.title: Delay and Cooperation in Nonstochastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative nonstochastic bandit on a communication network with common delay d (average welfare regret)
unmapped: N agents on a connected undirected communication graph G; messages (action, loss, distribution) propagate one hop per round and are dropped after d hops
Regret is the average welfare regret averaged over agents
Agents need not know G or N
settings.definition_quote: In our multi-agent bandit setting, there are N agents sitting on the vertices of a connected and undirected communication graph G = (V,E) ... R_T^{coop} = ( 1/N sum_{v} E[ sum_t loss_t(I_t(v)) ] - min_{i} sum_t loss_t(i) )

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative nonstochastic bandit with individual delays d(v) and time-to-live ttl(v)
unmapped: Each agent v uses individual delay d(v) and time-to-live ttl(v), inducing a directed communication graph G_P
Average welfare regret over N agents
settings.definition_quote: we analyze a modification of Exp3-Coop that allows each agent v in the network to use a delay parameter d(v) different from that of the other agents ... arc (v',v) in E_P if and only if dist_G(v,v') <= min{d(v),ttl(v')}.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-agent nonstochastic bandit with delayed losses (fixed delay d)
settings.definition_quote: a single agent is facing a bandit problem in which the loss of the chosen action is observed with a fixed delay d. In this setting, at the end of each round t the agent incurs loss loss_t(I_t) and observes loss_{t-d}(I_{t-d}), if t > d, and nothing otherwise.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-agent nonstochastic bandit with delayed losses (fixed delay d) (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: In the nonstochastic bandit setting with K >= 2 actions and delay d >= 0, where at the end of each round t the predictor has access to the losses loss_1(I_1),...,loss_s(I_s) for s = max{1,t-d}

algorithms.name: Exp3 with delayed updates (Exp3-Coop specialized to one agent)

symbols.alpha_d: independence number alpha(G_{<=d}) of the d-th power of the communication graph
symbols.gamma: learning-rate parameter in (0,1], eta = gamma/(K e (d+1))

source.label: th:nontuned
source.quote: The regret of Exp3-Coop run over a network G = (V,E) of N agents, each using delay d and learning rate \eta = \gamma/(Ke(d+1)), for \gamma \in (0,1], satisfies R_T^{coop} \le 2d + \frac{Ke(d+1)\ln K}{\gamma} + \gamma(\frac{\alpha(G_{\le d})}{2(1-e^{-1})(d+1)N} + \frac{3}{Ke})T.

results.notes: Paper's delay d mapped to D. Average welfare regret; oblivious adversary so E[loss] - min is expected regret.

bound.regime: T grows large (additive T-independent terms hidden)

symbols.alpha_d: independence number alpha(G_{<=d}) of the d-th power of the communication graph

tuning: individual learning rate eta(v) = gamma(v)/(K e (d+1)) chosen by local doubling trick

source.label: th:main
source.quote: The regret of Exp3-Coop run over a network G = (V,E) of N agents, each using delay d, and an individual learning rate \eta(v) = \gamma(v)/(Ke(d+1)), where \gamma(v) \in (0,1] is adaptively selected by each agent through the above doubling trick, satisfies, when T grows large, R_T^{coop} = O(\sqrt{(\ln K)(d + 1+ \frac{K}{N}\alpha(G_{\le d}))T} + d\log T).

results.notes: Remark: with d = sqrt(K), for any connected G this gives K^{1/4} sqrt(T ln K) + sqrt(K) ln T.

bound.regime: T grows large, eta -> 0 as T -> infinity

symbols.alpha_P: independence number of the directed graph G_P induced by delays and time-to-live

source.label: t:main-individual
source.quote: The regret of Exp3-Coop2 run over a network G = (V,E) of N agents, each agent v using individual delay d(v), individual time-to-leave ttl(v), exploration parameter \delta = 1/T, and learning rate \eta such that \eta \rightarrow 0 as T \rightarrow \infty satisfies, when T grows large, R_T^{coop} = O(\frac{\ln K}{\eta} + \eta({\bar d}_V + \frac{K}{N}\alpha(G_P)\ln(TNK))T)

results.notes: Proof also requires eta <= 1/(Ke(d(v)+1)) via Lemma; implicit for large T.

symbols.alpha_P: independence number of the directed graph G_P

tuning: individual learning rates eta(v) via doubling trick

source.label: c:main-individual-tuned
source.quote: The regret of Exp3-Coop2 run over a network G = (V,E) of N agents, each agent v using individual delay d(v), individual time-to-leave ttl(v), exploration parameter \delta = 1/T, and individual learning rate \eta(v) adaptively selected by each agent through a doubling trick, satisfies, when T grows large R_T^{coop} = O(\sqrt{(\ln K)({\bar d}_V + 1 + \frac{K}{N}\alpha(G_P)\ln(TNK))T} + {\bar d}_V(\ln T + \ln\ln(TNK))).

tuning: gamma chosen depending on T, K and d

source.label: c:delayed
source.quote: In the nonstochastic bandit setting with K \ge 2 actions and delay d \ge 0, where at the end of each round t the predictor has access to the losses \loss_1(I_1),\dots,\loss_s(I_s) for s = \max\{1,t-d\}, the minimax regret is of order \sqrt{(K + d)T}, ignoring logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Proof gives explicitly R_T = O(d + sqrt((K+d) T ln K)) by specializing Theorem th:nontuned with N=1.

source.label: c:delayed
source.quote: In the nonstochastic bandit setting with K \ge 2 actions and delay d \ge 0, ... the minimax regret is of order \sqrt{(K + d)T}, ignoring logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Proof shows max{sqrt(KT), sqrt((d+1)T ln K)} = Omega(sqrt((K+d)T)), combining Auer et al. bandit lower bound and Weinberger-Ordentlich delayed full-info reduction (asymptotic in K, B for the latter).
